narrative.overview:
A 440-logical-pixel tray panel that reads like a household meter: one grouped list, one 48px row per account, two thin bars per row. It adapts the macOS edition using native WPF controls and Segoe UI Variable. The old utility-style Windows interface is the anti-reference.

Density is calm. The Overview row carries a mini double ring, the account, a pace verdict and two numbers with bars (5h and Week); expanding it reveals the weekly pace chart. The window is opaque in light and dark, with Windows 11 rounded corners and no blur or transparency. Everything shown is provider-reported; there is no spend overview.
keyCharacteristics: Tonal layering, no shadows: depth comes from Background, Surface and Raised steps.
One purple accent, also the 5h window colour; Week uses a cyan data tone, not a second accent.
Alerts live in the number only; bars never change colour with severity.
Provider marks and the app mark are original SVG assets; interface icons are drawn strokes.
Light, dark and system themes share one token set; text scales 100, 110 or 125 percent as a single transform.

rules.name: The Number Alerts Rule
rules.body: Severity is carried by the number alone: red from 85 percent used, amber when the weekly projection passes 100 percent. Bars and rings keep their window colour.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is a single accent hue (purple). Cyan marks the Week window only and never labels providers, categories or actions.

rules.name: The High Contrast Rule
rules.body: When Windows high contrast is on, every role collapses to system window, text and highlight brushes.

rules.name: The Sentence Weight Rule
rules.body: Only SemiBold and Medium appear. Hardcoded titles use title case.

rules.name: The Scale Once Rule
rules.body: Text size 110 or 125 percent is one layout scale on the shell or dialog root; never also resize individual fonts.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces by background step and 1px Hairline, never by drop shadow or transparency.

dos: Do pull colors from the token roles and let the theme swap light and dark values.
Do put alerts in the number: red from 85 percent used, amber when the projection passes 100.
Do keep bars 3px with window colours (5h purple, Week cyan) regardless of severity.
Do name every interactive control for assistive technology and keep the focus ring visible.
Do use Windows-native input: keyboard focus, Escape closes dialogs, real controls.
Do show only provider-supplied values, and keep provider and account order as saved.
Do keep both themes, compact layouts, empty and error states, long account names and 125 percent text free of overlap at 400 to 500 px.
donts: Don't add a spend chart, spend overview, cost estimate or token tally; the product shows reported limits, balances, resets and weekly pace of reported percent only.
Don't add tooltips (hoverTooltip or WPF ToolTip).
Don't use drop shadows, gradient fills, blur or window transparency.
Don't introduce a second accent hue; cyan is reserved for the Week window.
Don't colour bars or rings by severity.
Don't revert to the old utility-style Windows interface.
Don't use hardcoded hex values in views; reference resource keys.
Don't show Density or Layout controls in Settings; they had no effect and were removed.
Don't make the keycaps look editable or add a shortcut recorder without wiring it.
Don't add shadows, translucency, Acrylic or tooltips to the Mini Widget or its flyout.
Don't put real account labels in shared review captures.
